name: jungle_depths_map_40x40
prompt:
16-bit pixel art, ONE single continuous top-down bomberman-style JUNGLE DEPTHS stage map, 40 by 40 square tiles, filling the entire square canvas edge to edge like a game board seen from directly above. This is NOT a selection sheet and NOT four panels: one uninterrupted map only. No outer frame, no margin, no labels, no text, no numbers, no UI, no characters, no watermark.

REFERENCE: the LEFT half shows the exact art style, palette and light level to match (pale fresh green, ancient tree courtyard, pale jade stone pavers, giant ancient tree trunks and roots, soft medium daylight). The RIGHT half is a flat layout guide; follow its PLACEMENT, density and proportions only. In the guide: dark green = dense giant trees and root border plus single tree props; orange = tree-type destructible blocks; purple = the 4x2 hollow ancient tree gate at the centre; blue = two clear shallow water ponds; cream = four open spawn plazas in the corners. Never copy the guide's flat colours, thin grid lines or blocky rectangles; render finished pixel-art props instead.

LAYOUT TO BUILD: a 2-cell-thick border of giant ancient trees and massive roots around the whole map; four open pale-stone spawn plazas in the four corners; two-cell-wide walkable cross paths from plaza to plaza; a central 8x8 open plaza holding one 4x2 hollow ancient tree-trunk gate as the landmark; two clear shallow ponds placed diagonally; about nine clusters of tree-type destructible blocks (2x2 each); a handful of single tree props and root runs breaking up the open ground. Every walkable cell must read clearly differently from every blocking cell.

TILE REUSE (strict): reuse a small set of tiles - only 3 floor variants (pale jade stone pavers, stone pavers overgrown with light grass, packed earth with leaf litter), only 4 tree wall props (young tree with round canopy, leafy bush, massive ancient root, cut stump), only 4 destructible tree-type block types (cut-log block, leafy sapling block, bush block, mossy stump block). Repeat them everywhere; do not invent a new tile for every cell. A few blocks carry a tiny carved snake-scale motif as a minor accent (4 blocks total, two of them pale green stone blocks with a simple snake relief).

STYLE: crisp hand-placed chunky pixels, 1px selective dark-green outline, flat cel shading with 2-3 tones, top-left light, soft medium brightness (not dark, not overexposed), fresh pale-green daylight, cream-white highlights, warm brown bark, thin dark green shadows only 1-2 tones darker, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no drop shadows, no isometric perspective, no 3D render.

GRID ALIGNMENT (strict, every prop): the map is exactly 40 by 40 cells, each cell 40 by 40 pixels. Every individual element - stone paver, grass tile, tree, bush, stump, log, brick block, pond edge - must sit exactly inside ONE grid cell with its base footprint centered on that cell: base midpoint = cell centre, base edges parallel to the cell edges. Tall props may rise above the cell, but their base may never drift horizontally or diagonally; nothing floats between cells and nothing straddles two cells. The only multi-cell prop is the central hollow tree gate, which covers exactly 4x2 whole cells with its base centered on that 4x2 block. No half-cell offsets, no squeezed or overlapping props.
